paragraphs: He is mentioned in the Jerusalem Talmud, Shabbat, chapter 1, end of halakhah 4, speaking in Rav Yirmeyah’s name.[^1][^2]

notes.text: The Guggenheimer digital text of Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 1:4 fully writes Rav Yirmeyah (רב ירמיה), supporting Rav for the supplied abbreviation ר׳. It has Zeira bar Avina, whereas the supplied heading has Avuna; that name form is retained.

The saved Guggenheimer Shabbat1:4 scalar has Rabbi Zeira bar Avina reporting Rav Yirmeyah. It supports body Rav Yirmeyah and the work locator. Hyman’s heading Avuna remains distinct from Avina; because the fuller qualifier differs, the heading abbreviation stays R' rather than transferring Rabbi. The older note’s description of Hyman as printing Rabbi is corrected: Hyman abbreviates.
